notes: IMDuel on Ethereum (chain 1): chess played by trades. ENGINE_ADDRESS is replaced by the ChessEngineV5 address from the engine launch (launch/engine.json) before this launch is opened. Constructor arguments in order: manager = $poolManager; engine = ChessEngineV5; imd = IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7; ethFee 10000 and ethSpacing 200: the hookless IMD / native ETH pool (id 0xb07d640fd9e2eb9dc81b953c8e4fd006bdfeaf276010fb5418eb763ca15abfb3) the ETH protocol slice is sold in; minImd 10 IMD, minEth 0.02 ETH, minImduel 1,000,000 IMDUEL: the smallest pile worth one conversion batch; turnBlocks 3: how many blocks a move takes bids for (a batch spends at most 10 minimums and one runs per block per pool; it buys within 0.1% of the most favourable of the sqrt prices its pool had at the start of the three latest sampled blocks, so a pushed price would have to be held through two public blocks; the main duel is sampled by its trades and batches, the IMD / ETH pool by each ETH batch). No owner, admin, pause or upgrade path. The first pool opened on the hook is the main duel and must pair IMD (afterInitialize reverts otherwise); its other currency becomes $IMDUEL. Every later duel must pair IMD, $IMDUEL or native ETH, so its slice can buy $IMDUEL (NoRoute otherwise). The token is src/IMDuelToken.sol on the standard terms (1,000,000,000 fixed, 18 decimals, the whole supply minted to the factory, plain transfers, no owner, mint, burn, tax, pause or blocklist). The factory deploys the hook, deploys the token and opens this pool in one transaction, so the factory's pool is always the main duel. The hook takes a 0.5% fee on every swap of its pools (0.4% to the pool's war chest worth less at the pool price, 0.1% protocol slice converted into $IMDUEL, half to the main duel's $IMDUEL chest, half sent to 0x...dEaD); for the main duel's first 300 seconds its chest share is up to 25% higher (falling linearly to 0.4%), all of it to the chest, against snipers at launch (time only, nothing per wallet; duels opened later don't have it) through beforeSwapReturnDelta / afterSwapReturnDelta; it leaves the 1.25% LP fee untouched. A swap must trade its whole order (the fee part taken before the swap counts all of it): one its price limit stops early reverts (PartialFill). Liquidity callbacks are not used. Every buy bids for its team's next move: the biggest owns it and a new top bid must pay more than 10% over the current one; a move takes bids for turnBlocks blocks (3, about 36 seconds) after the previous one was played (or until its first bid if none came by then), and the first swap after its window plays it through a gas-capped external call to the engine, seeded by the hash of the window's last block (BLOCKHASH, or the EIP-2935 history contract 0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935 beyond 256 blocks; a turn whose hash is no longer served becomes a 0% timeout turn). An engine failure never reverts a swap; an engine starved by the swap's own gas limit reverts it (NotEnoughGas) so gas estimates include the move.
